issues.legal_issue: A prior refusal to discharge an accused does not bar a renewed discharge application when the court had expressly preserved liberty to seek discharge after pre-charge evidence was recorded.
A prima facie case for proceeding to trial must rest on material indicating the essential ingredients of the alleged offence, rather than on a bare suspicion or an unsupported conclusion.

The statutory presumption under Section 20 of the Prevention of Corruption Act arises only after foundational facts establishing demand and acceptance or obtainment of illegal gratification have been proved, and cannot arise from allegations alone.

Misuse of official authority or deviation from government policy, without material alleging demand and acceptance or obtainment of illegal gratification, does not by itself establish an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Criminal proceedings under the Prevention of Corruption Act cannot continue against an accused where the investigation report and pre-charge evidence disclose no allegation or material of that accused’s demand or acceptance of illegal gratification.
